title: Surjectivity on first Tor after a flat intermediate base change
statement: Let $R\to A\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings and $M$ an $R$-module. Assume $M\otimes_RA$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then the natural $B$-linear map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)\otimes_AB\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,B)$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], induced by $A\to B$ in the second variable, is surjective.

proof.text: Choose a free resolution $\cdots\to F_2\to F_1\to F_0\to M\to0$ over $R$. The complexes $F_\bullet\otimes_R A$ and $F_\bullet\otimes_R B$ compute the two Tor groups in the statement by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Put $K_A=\ker(F_1\otimes_R A\to F_0\otimes_R A)$ and define $K_B$ similarly; then $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,B)$ are the corresponding cycle modules modulo the images of $F_2$.

Put $I=\operatorname{im}(F_1\otimes_R A\to F_0\otimes_R A)$. The exact augmented sequence splits at $I$ into $0\to K_A\to F_1\otimes_R A\to I\to0$ and $0\to I\to F_0\otimes_R A\to M\otimes_R A\to0$. Since $M\otimes_R A$ is flat over $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] applied to the second short exact sequence makes $I\otimes_A B\to F_0\otimes_R B$ injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to the first, $K_A\otimes_A B\to F_1\otimes_R B\to I\otimes_A B\to0$ is exact. The identifications $(F_i\otimes_R A)\otimes_A B\cong F_i\otimes_R B$ identify the latter map with the map induced by $F_1\otimes_R B\to F_0\otimes_R B$; therefore the image of $K_A\otimes_A B$ is $K_B$ and the induced map $K_A\otimes_A B\twoheadrightarrow K_B$ is surjective.

By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], tensoring the quotient presentation $F_2\otimes_R A\to K_A\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)\to0$ with $B$ gives a quotient of $K_A\otimes_A B$ identified with $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)\otimes_A B$. The map $F_2\otimes_R B\to K_B$ is the base change of the corresponding map over $A$, so the surjection $K_A\otimes_A B\twoheadrightarrow K_B$ descends to a surjection on these quotients. The $A$-module structure on $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)$ is the functorial one in the second variable; on pure tensors the induced map sends $\bar k\otimes b$ to the class of $b\bar k$, hence this descended map is the natural map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)\otimes_A B\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,B)$ from [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. It is therefore surjective. Lean interface repair R1: torOneModule is constructed by applying the second-variable Tor functor to multiplication endomorphisms. torOneCoefficientMap is that functor applied to the algebra map. torOneBaseChange is the balanced tensor lift of (t,b) ↦ b • torOneCoefficientMap(t), with B-linearity and its pure-tensor formula proved. The surjectivity argument above remains to be formalized; no proof of that argument is claimed. The canonical module laws use additivity of the coefficient functor [lem-weil-pbc-tor-one-second-additive]; its restriction-of-scalars compatibility uses R-linearity [lem-weil-pbc-tor-one-second-linear]. These supporting results are already proved in this module, independently of the remaining surjectivity hole.
